svg.title: Portable definitions. Target-local data.
svg.desc: All five Git-owned Fabric items travel together with portable logical IDs. An explicitly attached Bootstrap plan synchronizes the published branch into DEV. Review and commit generated DEV binding changes before freezing the source and promoting reviewed live definitions to initially empty TEST through the native DEV/TEST pipeline. TEST must bind and verify its own data. PROD is separately provisioned and governed by the derived project. Within an attached DEV/TEST Bootstrap plan, the four ordered groups deploy Scenario, deploy and execute SeedScenario, deploy ScenarioOntology, then deploy and execute BindScenario. Git and pipelines copy definitions, not OneLake data. Production uses a separately reviewed plan with approved ingestion instead of demo seeding. A Git push alone does not run the plan.

g.text: Native Git bootstraps DEV; pipelines promote reviewed business definitions.
Five Git items. Logical IDs stay portable; physical bindings are resolved in each target.
Inside an attached DEV/TEST Bootstrap plan
Explicit dependencies. Each notebook is deployed before its action runs.
No OneLake data is copied by Git/pipelines.
Each target owns its data and source bindings.
PROD has a separate release plan.
Omit demo seeding; use approved ingestion.
Do not weaken the DEV/TEST seed guard.
A Git push does not run Bootstrap. Attach the reviewed plan and wait for its actions.
